insight: When adding tests that use async/Promise-returning handlers in mock fetch implementations, always verify the mock's dispatch function actually awaits handler results. The mcp-fake-server.ts mock had a synchronous `handle()` function that silently swallowed Promise-returning handlers (returning `{ result: <Promise> }` which serialized to empty), causing timeout tests to see `[]` instead of timing out. This was a latent bug that only surfaced when the new spawnTimeoutMs tests introduced async handlers. When a test fails with an unexpected empty result instead of the expected error/timeout, suspect the mock isn't awaiting async handlers. Also: AbortSignal support in mock fetch must reject the returned Promise (not just check signal.aborted after the fact) for timeout tests to work — the wrapper pattern with addEventListener('abort') is the correct approach.
